## What is already there

BAD-080's rule: a collab room in `wrapping` becomes `wrapped` **on read**, so between the booth's stop beat and a take's last `commit`, a client must say nothing to the room but the delivery itself (`upload-url` and `commit` are the only two modes `collab/room.ts` stands aside on). The change took the `info` read off the push path in both clients, held the booth's *idle* heartbeat while a take is owed (`collabIdleBeat` / `collabTakeInFlight()`), and made `main.js`'s 60s info poller skip a room in `collabDelivering`.

A review (Yukon, BADS-080/Yukon — `spud member show BADS-080/Yukon` for the full evidence) confirmed all seven of that design's load-bearing claims, including the server ordering it rests on: `collab/index.ts:113` runs `loadRoom` — the `completeWrap` probe — before `:122` dispatches `heartbeat`, and `seats.ts:33-38` is the only write to `recording_at`. None of that needs revisiting.

## The gap to close

A **pre-existing 20s focus poll** in each client calls `refreshCollab(…, { pull: false })`, which opens an unconditional `info` read, whenever the collab is active and the booth is visible — that is, throughout every delivery. It was never gated, and it is the last way a client still wraps a room under its own take.

- `renderer/app.js:4858-4864` — the `setInterval` on `COLLAB_FOCUS_POLL_MS`, guarded only by `collabFocusedRoomVisible()`.
- `web/collabweb.js:117-123` — `collab.focusTimer`, guarded only by the modal-hidden / `state.view !== 'booth'` check.

Gate both poll bodies with **exactly the predicate `collabIdleBeat` already uses**: skip the tick when the recorder is not recording and `collabTakeInFlight()` is true. Same rule, same words, both clients — do not invent a second spelling of it. If `collabTakeInFlight` is not in scope at either call site, export or hoist it rather than writing the condition out again; the whole point of BAD-089 (already filed) is that this rule is duplicated too much already, so do not add a third copy.

Skip the tick, do not defer it — the next tick is twenty seconds away and a delivery is seconds, which is the reasoning `main.js`'s poller already states.

`web/collabweb.js` was outside the previous member's deliverables, which is why nothing caught this. It is inside yours.

## Ticket proposals
- **npm run web:local leaves the local collab flag on, which fails the server suite's flag_off case** — suggested P3; created as [[BAD-092]] at P2 by Spud.
  Why: scripts/web-local.js runs 'update private.feature_flags set default_value = true where key = collab' and never puts it back, so any later run of test/server/functions.test.mjs against the same stack fails. The suite's own comment at :2517 says the flag is seeded OFF on a fresh stack and guards against a leaked targeting RULE dropped in a finally -- but nothing guards against default_value itself having been flipped, which is the one thing the web dev loop does on purpose. Two documented tools on one shared stack that silently break each other.
  Evidence: Hit it in this worktree today. Ran 'npm run web:local' for BAD-080's end-to-end, then npm test with functions served: one failure, 'expected { error: flag_off, code: flag_off }, actual { error: not_a_member, code: not_a_member }' at test/server/functions.test.mjs:2744 -- the flag being on lets the request past the wall and into the membership check. Verified the cause directly: 'select key, default_value from private.feature_flags' reads collab|t, while migration 0015_collab_flag.sql:13 seeds it false. Same failure will greet anyone who runs the server suite on this machine until someone sets it back; I was refused permission to write to the shared DB, so it is still on as I finish. Options: have web-local.js restore the prior value on exit, have the suite assert/reset default_value the way it already drops its rule, or say plainly in server/README.md that the two cannot share a stack.
